title: Pay a multicore off a free-turning drum to its cradle without leaving the drum running unheld
instruction: Pay the red cable off the drum along the yellow-taped run and rest its connector in the white cradle, then let go.
context: Ability: pacing a pull on a free-spinning cable reel and handing the cable between hands without the reel turning unheld. Electricians (O*NET 47-2111.00) "pull insulated wires or cables through the conduit to complete circuits between boxes"; cable comes off a reel or drum that turns as it is pulled. The reel is a small 12 cm one with no brake, so the pull is paced.
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). Drum on a vertical axle at x 29, y 31: grey hub 5 cm diameter, 7 cm tall, 0.4 kg, with a grey 12 cm, 0.3 kg top flange and a white 110 x 12 mm bar across it. Cable: red 6 mm round PVC multicore, 64 cm, inner end fixed to the hub, wound clockwise from above, about 2.5 turns; the tail lies out toward the right, black 35 x 16 x 12 mm connector at x 32.5, y 14.5. Yellow tape: two 1 x 45 cm lines, 8 cm apart inside, from (37.7, 25.4) to (45.4, -18.9) and (28.9, 23.9) to (36.5, -20.5). White cradle centred at x 41.4, y -23.2, axis along the run: 48 x 22 mm seat, walls 12 mm tall and 6 mm thick, 10 mm cable slot.
scoring: Score 0 if at any time: the drum turns over 360 deg/s; or over 20 deg/s while no gripper pinches the cable or connector (finger gap stopped at the part's width, -4/+2 mm, with the part between the pads; a gripper shut on nothing or hovering near the cable does not count); or a wound turn stands over 2 cm off the coil. Also 0 if at the end a gripper is within 3 cm of the cable or connector, or the connector centre is not in the cradle seat on the table. 0.5: connector seated, but cable over 6 cm from the axle outside the tape lines or past the cradle, or drum over 3 deg/s. 1.0: seated, cable between the tapes, drum still; ends after 1 s of this.
reset_notes: Wind the cable back onto the hub clockwise (from above), turns tight, until the connector lies at x 32.5, y 14.5 cm; lay the tail on the table; check the drum is still.
fidelity: Cable: 2 cm rigid segments with bending springs, no twist. It keeps a coil set while on the drum and lies straight once paid out. The drum turns on a damped axle (about 1e-3 N m s/rad) and coasts about 1 s after a fast pull, throwing the coil loose. In real trials drum speed comes from the white bar on video, holding from fingers stopped on the part, the loose turn from a ruler against the coil. No drum brake: the pull itself must be paced. Connector is a rigid box.
